wbs: Confirm one-way Excel-to-Odoo product-import scope, assumptions, objectives, limits and acceptance targets.
Approved scope baseline and decision log.
Interview or structured-review the instructor, an ERP data-entry user and Odoo administrator; record needs and constraints.
Requirements and stakeholder register updated with evidence.
Profile Excel data and Odoo product fields
Inspect representative rows, required columns, types, duplicate SKU patterns and target Odoo fields.
Data profile, sample file and field inventory.
Verify sandbox availability, authentication, permissions and one safe test write; document fallback if unavailable.
Connection proof or a documented no-access decision.
Approve data dictionary and acceptance criteria
Specify source-to-target fields, validation rules, duplicate policy and measurable acceptance evidence.
Define file intake, validation, mapping, Odoo adapter, batch handling, logging and extension points.
Define credential handling, least privilege, safe retry boundaries, idempotency key and manual reconciliation state.
Read the agreed .xlsx template and produce normalized product records with source row references.
Check required fields, numeric types, allowed values and duplicates in file or target; reject unsafe rows.
Validation service with actionable row-level errors.
Map normalized records to target product fields using an editable mapping configuration.
Mapping module and documented field map.
Implement the selected API adapter and isolated credential configuration for the test environment.
Adapter can create an allowed test product and return a target identifier.
Build batch orchestration and audit log
Process rows independently, capture status and correlation IDs, and place ambiguous outcomes into reconciliation.
Batch result report with success, rejection and uncertain states.
Provide a simple command or minimal screen to select a file, start a batch and inspect results.
Repeatable operator workflow and example configuration.
Prepare test plan and test data
Prepare 12 scenario-based cases and a synthetic product file, including invalid, duplicate and API-failure cases.
Approved test cases and synthetic input data.
Test parser, validation, mapping, duplicate detection and adapter behavior in isolation.
Test execution log and defect list.
Test the full path against a safe Odoo sandbox and verify target records and logs.
Evidence for each case, including retry/reconciliation behavior.
Fix defects and repeat failed tests
Prioritize defects by data loss, duplicate creation, blocking errors and usability; rerun affected cases.
Closed or accepted defect list and retest evidence.
Demonstrate valid import, rejected rows, duplicate prevention and traceable outcome to the reviewer.
Acceptance record or documented open issues.
Control the project and report progress
Maintain MS Project baseline, issue/decision log, weekly status, scope control and risk review across 12 weeks.
Updated schedule, dashboard, change log and meeting notes.
Document prerequisites, configuration, safe test procedure, results and known limitations.
Guide that another member can follow.
Prepare final report, slides and demo
Connect project evidence to the assignment criteria and distinguish actual test results from estimates.
Review acceptance, remaining risks, effort variance and reusable learning.

risks: Odoo API access or permissions unavailable
Sandbox, API capability or service-account rights do not support the required safe write.
Prototype integration cannot be demonstrated.
Technical architect
Run a connection proof by Week 2. If blocked, use a controlled mock for development and label real Odoo connection as not verified.
No successful authenticated test write by end of Week 2.
High
Data quality and field mapping are harder than planned
Excel formats vary; product fields or required relationships are unclear.
Import rejects many records or creates incorrect product data.
PM / BA
Profile sample data early; freeze one template; keep invalid rows out of Odoo; get a domain reviewer to approve mapping.
More than 10% of sample rows require manual interpretation.
High
Scope expands beyond the MVP
Requests add two-way sync, more ERP systems, extra records or real-time behavior.
Schedule and testing capacity become insufficient.
Project Manager
Use a change log and impact estimate; defer additions unless scope, schedule and acceptance are re-approved.
Any new system, data entity or direction is requested after Week 3.
High
Duplicate or incorrect Odoo records are created
Retry after an uncertain response or weak duplicate key causes repeated creates.
Data integrity is affected and demo evidence becomes unreliable.
Technical architect
Use a stable import/batch key, reject existing SKUs, test timeout-after-commit and keep uncertain outcomes for manual reconciliation.
Same import reference is submitted twice or result is unknown after timeout.
High
Key member availability drops
Course workload, illness or schedule conflict reduces contribution.
Critical activities wait for one person; review and testing are compressed.
Project Manager
Assign a backup for connector and testing; maintain weekly work cap and shared runbook; level resources in MS Project.
A critical task has no active owner for one week.
Medium
Credentials or test data are exposed
Secrets are committed or real customer/vendor data is used in development.
Unauthorized access or privacy impact.
Technical architect
Use synthetic data; store secrets outside source control; restrict sandbox rights; rotate exposed credentials.
Secret appears in repository, screenshot or shared report.
Medium
Effort estimate is too optimistic
Early assumptions omit mapping, failure handling, documentation or integration tests.
Forecast exceeds available 12-week capacity.
Project Manager
Use PERT ranges and a 15% contingency reserve; compare actual hours weekly; escalate at SPI below 0.90.
Actual effort exceeds plan by 10% at a milestone.
Medium
End-to-end tests fail late
Components are developed in isolation and API contract differences surface near integration.
Retesting and fixing consume handover time.
QA / documentation
Create a thin end-to-end slice by Week 5; run sandbox integration at least weekly; reserve Weeks 10–11 for fixes.
More than two critical integration defects remain at Week 9.
Medium

sources: Schwalbe, K. (2019). Information Technology Project Management, 9th ed. Cengage.
Theory for charter, scope, schedule, cost, resources, communications, risk and stakeholders.
https://www.cengage.com/c/information-technology-project-management-9e-schwalbe/
Silva, J. P., Silva, N., & Rocha, J. (2011). Online, iterative and interactive integration of legacy system and up-to-date ERP: a case study and systematization. INFORUM 2011.
Single SME integration case

Case reports a 35-hour one-person-week expectation, a two-person-week unsuccessful pilot, and data-quality transformations that could not handle about 20% of 2,702 records. Used as a cautionary analogy for early profiling, broad effort ranges and a test buffer; not a direct estimate for this much smaller student MVP.
https://www.academia.edu/7322292/Online_iterative_and_interactive_integration_of_legacy_system_and_up-to-date_ERP_a_case_study_and_systematization
Rosa, W. et al. (2013). COTS integration and estimation for ERP. Journal of Systems and Software, 86(2), 538–550.
20 US federal ERP programs

Study links RICE object counts to integration effort and schedule. Its model population and size range differ from a single educational connector, so the model is not numerically applied; the project uses interface/data-conversion/test-object decomposition instead. DOI: 10.1016/j.jss.2012.09.030.
Kong, X. (2025). User-Centered Design of an ERP Integration Framework for Trading SMEs: Customizing Microsoft Dynamics 365 BC and Integrating Lark. Aalto University thesis.
Architecture and user-centered design reference
A related project context for user-centered ERP integration. The official thesis title listing is used only for contextual comparison, not as an effort benchmark.
https://aaltodoc.aalto.fi/items/89435701-13ac-48f7-90df-4283e1a429fd
User-supplied draft Khoa_luan_ERP_Integration_Framework.docx (27 pages; local Library item)
Project design draft; simulated evidence only

Draft describes SME Bridge Lab, transactional outbox, worker, idempotency, mock ERP and 12 tests/180 synthetic orders. It explicitly states the Odoo adapter is unverified on a live Odoo server and mock results are not field evidence. Used as a design input, not independent project data.
